items.note: NHS: call when contractions are regular and coming every 5 minutes or more often. Measured start to start.

items.note: The NHS call-for-advice wording gives no duration, so the UK default is off (0). If a midwife gives a duration it can be set between 30 and 90 seconds.

items.note: NHS says 'regular' without giving a time. One hour matches the widely used 5-1-1 convention. Can be shortened, never lengthened.

provenance.sourceTitle: NHS: Signs that labour has begun

items.note: NHS: call urgently if any contraction lasts longer than 2 minutes. Can be tightened, never relaxed.

provenance.sourceTitle: NHS: Signs that labour has begun

items.note: NHS: call urgently if there are 6 or more contractions in 10 minutes. NICE defines tachysystole as more than 5 in 10 minutes, so 5 is the tightest setting.

items.note: App-defined, for midwife review. Turns 'regular' into a number: the spread of start-to-start intervals (interquartile range) divided by the median interval.

items.note: Second and later babies, a previous fast labour or a journey over 30 minutes: call earlier rather than waiting the full hour. Not editable in v1.
